title: Nominick Hills
summary: Nominick is connected with hills on Montauk in East Hampton, where the high land rises out of the sandy and marshy Neapeague. The placename is remembered through traditional usage and later local writing rather than early town records.
history_content: The placename brings together the Nominick Hills location, remembered spelling forms, and Montauk landscape context. Dated source mentions appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Nummonok, Naumunack, Nommonock, Nominick, and Nomnick. The interpretation is land to be seen afar off, connected with words meaning to see or to be seen.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names can communicate history, a description of place, and connection to the land.”

— Anna Moffat, Traditional Ecological Knowledge in Indigenous Language Revitalization (2024), PDF page 25
whereintheworld_content: Approximate general point in the Hither Hills / Nominick Hills area at the eastern edge of Neapeague. The map placement is for orientation only, not an exact hill boundary, fort location, or archaeological coordinate. Offset slightly from the nearby Fresh Pond Fort marker for map visibility.
